status_note: LIVE labels describe operational research maturity, not verified actual performance.

entries.name: BASE
entries.description: Engine / governed spine / systematic risk structure
entries.finding: Predictive-return tests failed, but diversification and trend premia persisted out of sample. The spine has also completed the governed path from data through orders and reconciliation.

entries.name: BRICS
entries.finding: The broad BRICS basket was mostly emerging-market beta, but the Gulf pocket supplied genuinely lower correlation. A dollar overlay materially reduced drawdown and improved risk-adjusted return.

entries.name: BONDS
entries.finding: The stock–bond correlation regime was detectable ahead of time even though the other predictive components were null. That makes BONDS useful as a portfolio overlay and signal emitter, not a standalone trade.

entries.name: BROAD
entries.finding: Leveraged wrappers lost their appeal once risk was matched. Unlevered QQQ with trend and volatility targeting preserved participation while controlling drawdown. The edge was exposure management, not leverage.

entries.name: BOOM
entries.finding: Twelve-to-one momentum captured persistent mega-cap leadership. Position caps and volatility targeting made the result governable, though dependence on a few winners keeps concentration risk explicit.

entries.name: BENCHMARK
entries.finding: Market internals mostly coincided with stress rather than leading it, but volatility regimes persisted long enough to inform sizing. BENCHMARK therefore emits a bounded risk input instead of claiming new alpha.

entries.name: BULL
entries.finding: Raw growth exposure was largely beta. Conditioning it on the rate regime improved Sharpe, skew, and drawdown enough to make that beta ownable within a governed portfolio.

entries.name: BRIDGEWATER
entries.finding: All Weather remained a valid low-volatility compounder, although it was highly correlated with the existing spine. The recognized allocation was retained as a governed book; a redundant overlay was not.

entries.name: BLACKSTONE
entries.finding: Listed private equity proved to be leveraged, procyclical equity and credit exposure, not a hedge. A market-regime overlay cut drawdown enough to turn that transparent factor into a usable governed sleeve.

entries.name: BRASH
entries.finding: Aggression multiplied both growth and ruin; full Kelly and beyond deepened drawdown without improving the underlying edge. Fractional Kelly with volatility targeting preserved the return source within explicit risk limits.

entries.name: BOUNCE
entries.finding: Fading the index failed, but ten-day cross-sectional reversal remained modestly positive in choppy regimes and near market-neutral. The edge is relative dislocation, not a broad-market call.

entries.name: BLUE
entries.finding: Static ownership of either thematic camp underperformed. Relative trend between the camps added value, making rotation rather than permanent allegiance the investable finding.

entries.name: BROWN
entries.finding: The conservative and real-asset camp was not a superior static holding. Its value emerged only when relative trend rotated exposure between Brown and Blue regimes.

entries.name: BITDOLLAR
entries.description: Governed BTC / ETH trend and volatility targeting
entries.finding: Trend and volatility targeting retained much of crypto's upside while sharply reducing its deepest loss. The dollar-axis thesis was rejected; disciplined exposure control was the survivor.

entries.name: BOTTOM
entries.description: Drawdown bounce / liquidity and cap-ladder discipline
entries.finding: Moving down the capitalization ladder added idiosyncratic risk and trading cost rather than edge. Liquid large-cap drawdown bounces were the only version robust enough to keep.

entries.name: BORE
entries.finding: Hedging removed the flattering market beta but left a smaller, real momentum residue. Used as portable alpha over an index, it improved the portfolio rather than pretending neutrality was free.

entries.name: BLUNT
entries.finding: Five short-horizon ideas failed; a one-day crude-to-refiner lead–lag remained. The result rewards observed follow-through in a linked market rather than trading the headline itself.

entries.name: BLEED
entries.finding: Static long volatility carried too much annual cost. A diversified basket covering both inflationary and deflationary crises delivered negative crisis correlation with tolerable carry, so it earned a role as insurance.

entries.name: BEYOND
entries.finding: Very short horizons reversed while horizons beyond roughly twenty days became momentum. Long winners survived; acceleration did not, and overlap with BOOM limits the sleeve's independent weight.

entries.name: APAC
entries.finding: Unhedged regional exposure was mostly US beta plus FX drag. Cross-country relative strength was the durable pulse, provided the implementation remains hedged or dollar-neutral.

entries.name: BANKROLL
entries.finding: Naive buy-write is a drag, but selective, calm-gated writing (DIVO) clears the hurdle with the upside intact — the first sell-side sleeve to escape 'insurance-selling, not alpha.'

entries.name: BOROUGH
entries.finding: A low-vol, tax-advantaged carry stream (~+3.3% tax-equivalent) that beats Treasuries for taxable capital; the edge is the exemption, not pre-tax alpha, so it is a conditional keeper.

entries.name: BRIER
entries.description: Prediction-market order-flow + the gate's ground truth
entries.finding: Binary contracts resolve 0/1, so pricing error is observable — the one market where the random-entry gate can be checked against known truth. The gate shows power (fires on real order-flow impact) and specificity (silent on noise); the live tradable edge is parked on data (brier_2).

entries.name: BINNACLE
entries.description: LDI duration-matching / immunize the funded ratio
entries.finding: Matching asset duration to a long liability drives funded-ratio volatility toward zero; core bonds and equity leave large surplus risk. Risk elimination, not a return edge - and 2022 showed under-hedging is a rate bet. The liability capstone's stabilizer.

entries.name: BARBELL
entries.description: Taleb convexity / safe core + convex sliver
entries.finding: The two-wing barbell (cash + levered equity + long-vol) dominates a 60/40 on Sharpe (+1.58), Calmar (+0.98), skew (+0.63) and a -4% drawdown - convexity done right beats the mediocre middle, at the cost of absolute return. Antifragile, green in every crisis.

entries.name: BREAKTHROUGH
entries.finding: Risk parity over the validated keepers, paired with conditional insurance, converted many separate findings into one diversified and governable portfolio rather than another prediction.

entries.name: BRILLIANT
entries.finding: Minimum-variance and maximum-Sharpe optimization cleared the index hurdle, but neither reliably beat risk parity. Covariance information was useful; precise return forecasts were not.

entries.name: BOSSY
entries.finding: Concentrating conviction worsened risk-adjusted results. Modest leverage on diversified risk parity raised return without inventing a new edge, while making the deeper drawdown explicit.

entries.name: BELIEVER
entries.finding: Buying and holding the keepers was already strong, but drift recreated concentration. Rebalancing by risk budget improved the portfolio, showing that allocation discipline matters after selection.

entries.name: BEMUSED
entries.description: Random-allocation null / the edge is the keepers
entries.finding: Random allocations of validated keepers were already strong, while BREAKTHROUGH ranked near the top of the distribution. Most value came from ingredient quality; allocation skill was real but smaller.

entries.name: BRIGADE
entries.finding: Adding carefully selected, low-correlation void-fillers improved risk-adjusted return. Breadth helped only when each addition filled a portfolio need rather than repeating an existing bet.

entries.name: BOUNDLESS
entries.description: Kitchen-sink capstone / more is not better
entries.finding: Adding every near-keeper diluted the portfolio because correlated ingredients could not manufacture diversification. The control proves that curation, not maximal breadth, is the allocation edge.

entries.name: BASTION
entries.description: Insurance capstone / a null rehabilitated by −corr
entries.finding: A weak standalone bear sleeve became valuable at a small portfolio weight because its negative correlation reduced drawdown. Portfolio contribution, rather than standalone return, earned its place.

entries.name: BALSAMIC
entries.finding: A managed-futures trend satellite complemented the risk-parity core across different regimes. The combined book improved resilience and passed the governed dry-run without duplicating the core.

entries.name: BULKHEAD
entries.description: Preservation capstone / family-office book + convex tail
entries.finding: The FO-mandate book — low-vol equity, muni, gold and a long-vol tail. Beats 60/40, all-weather and the aggressive book on every preservation axis (Sharpe +1.20, maxDD -12%, the only positive-skew book), giving up CAGR. The tail layer flips the skew.

entries.name: BELLIGERENT
entries.finding: Levers the return-seeking keepers (QQQ/MTUM/GLD/EMB), vol-targeted to 18%. Beats SPY on CAGR (+19.3%), Sharpe (+1.02) and Calmar at a -30% drawdown, and crushes naive 3x leverage (-77% DD). The edge is disciplined leverage, not alpha.

entries.name: BACKSTOP
entries.finding: LDI hedge + spread carry + plain-equity growth + a convex tail. Earns +5.9%/yr surplus over the liability at a funded-ratio drawdown of -22% (vs a naive 60/40's -37%), positive skew, crisis-convex. Funds the obligations without betting the funded ratio on rates.

entries.name: BRAWL
entries.description: Economics horse-race / doctrine books by P&L
entries.finding: Builds the book each economic school prescribes and scores by P&L. No doctrine wins outright: on return Behavioral = Chicago (behavioral is beta); risk-adjusted goes to Austrian (gold's decade). The race crowns whoever's asset had the decade - regime-dependence wearing a philosophy.

entries.name: BODEGA
entries.description: Dealer book / sell-side: be the house
entries.finding: Sells income, structure and insurance for a steady carry (+6.9%/yr) but is structurally short convexity (skew -1.24) - the counterparty to the preservation books. Slightly dominated by a 60/40; the real dealer edge (franchise, flow, balance sheet) isn't replicable in ETFs.

entries.name: BEAR
entries.description: Regime-gated short / costly incomplete tail insurance
entries.finding: The gated short still paid persistent carry and covered only part of major crashes. A coincident regime signal cannot reliably time the short, and BLEED already provides broader protection.

entries.name: BALANCED
entries.description: Value factor / rate sensitivity / margin-of-safety test
entries.finding: Value behaved largely as a rate-sensitive factor: volatility fell, but crashes remained and growth led over the test period. It may be a conditional ingredient, not a durable standalone edge.

entries.name: BOGLE
entries.description: Low-cost index hurdle / factor and fund comparison
entries.finding: None of the tested Vanguard tilts reliably beat the low-cost index on a risk-adjusted basis. Apparent winners were mostly beta, making BOGLE the hurdle every active idea must clear.

entries.name: BUFFETT
entries.finding: The factor decomposition was coherent, but neither the public factors nor Berkshire reliably beat the index in the recent sample. Selection and cheap float appear central, and the proxies do not fully capture them.

entries.name: BASKET
entries.description: Exchange funds / tax-deferral and estate vehicle
entries.finding: The vehicle creates no alpha; its value is tax deferral under narrow conditions: large embedded gains, low fees, and a long holding period. Suitability depends more on the owner than the market.

entries.name: BLOCK
entries.finding: Cross-asset lead–lag relationships were too weak to trade reliably. The durable output is the governed four-block allocation, supported by an open derivatives reference rather than a single predictive sleeve.

entries.name: BOMBS AWAY
entries.description: Fragility monitor / tail-hedge sizing / not a crash timer
entries.finding: The fragility tells describe building stress but do not predict forward drawdowns or sudden shocks. The monitor survives only as a bounded tail-hedge sizing input, not a market-timing switch.

entries.name: BALLAST
entries.description: Dollar-neutral construction vs post-hoc beta removal
entries.finding: Building beta-neutrality in beats regressing it out after the fact, which over-corrects; a conditional keeper that scopes the full reinforcement-learning go/no-go still to be run.

entries.name: BAZAAR
entries.finding: A real carry stream (EMB cleanest) but substantially a short-dollar bet with a crash-correlated tail that overlaps the BRICS dollar regime.

entries.name: BLEND
entries.finding: The crack spread is an independent, positive-skew diversifier (+0.43 Sharpe), but its return is realized margin expansion, not carry, and crush/spark need a futures feed.

entries.name: BOULDER
entries.finding: A genuinely uncorrelated diversifier that pays in slow bears, but the positive-skew crisis convexity is absent on ETF proxies and needs a futures universe.

entries.name: BRAID
entries.finding: Laddering removes single-date timing luck and the delta-strikes keep upside, but it is a steadier buy-write, not new alpha.

entries.name: BREACH
entries.finding: Real and out-of-sample stable, and sharper than a plain vol-state, but it forecasts magnitude not direction — a risk/sizing flag, not alpha.

entries.name: BULLION
entries.description: Gold miners vs metal relative value
entries.finding: Miners are ~1.9x-levered gold with an idiosyncratic drag, but the market-neutral GDX/GLD ratio RV (+0.61 Sharpe) is a real conditional sleeve.

entries.name: BULWARK
entries.finding: The dynamic anchor's crash-dodge is confirmed and material — it halves the left skew — but it buys the calm with foregone return versus plain momentum.

entries.name: BURDENSOME
entries.finding: Real, compensated, and partly distinct from selling puts, but a specialty-equity bet with full market beta and a worse drawdown; a later mirage audit downgraded the distinct-premium claim to fragile.

entries.name: BUSHEL
entries.finding: Raw short-vol is a landmine; a term-structure gate shrinks the crater but cannot remove the tail — conditional insurance-selling, the mirror of the TAIL sleeve, not alpha.

entries.name: BIDIRECTIONAL
entries.finding: Contrarian at bottoms and momentum-confirmation at tops hold up, but only as a regime rule — fade solely under tightening — not a symmetric standalone sleeve.

entries.name: BACKWARDS
entries.finding: Vol-scaling's skew repair is momentum-specific as claimed, but immaterial in-sample because the 2009 crash predates the data window.

entries.name: BUTTRESS
entries.description: Convex tail hedge on levered momentum
entries.finding: Adding a convex hedge to levered momentum is Sharpe-neutral (+0.80 vs +0.79): the hedge is a risk choice, not an edge — null for alpha, conditional as insurance.

entries.name: BARGAIN
entries.finding: The discount-reversion edge shows up on a price proxy (+0.87 Sharpe) but needs a NAV feed to be real, and the tradable PCEF basket does not beat 60/40.

entries.name: BARREL
entries.finding: The contango bleed is the headline (avoid front-month ETFs); a clean roll-carry harvest needs a futures term structure to test, so the verdict is conditional/null-ish.

entries.name: BRIEF
entries.finding: The equity premium genuinely lives overnight, but it is un-harvestable net of a daily round-trip and the seasonal tilts have decayed — an honest execution insight, not a sleeve.

entries.name: BEZEL
entries.finding: Buffered/defined-outcome ETFs sell a buffer for a cap. The autopsy: it's symmetric beta-reduction dressed as asymmetry (up-capture ~ down-capture), and the fee lives in forgone dividends + the cap - a plain SPY+cash mix replicates it near-free. BLOCK's 'where the fee lives', made tradable.

entries.name: BRAVADO
entries.description: Hall-of-fame audit / edge vs convexity-luck vs ruin
entries.finding: The celebrated unorthodox bets, sorted by tail sign: convex winners (Big Short, Taleb) paid once and can't be timed; steady-Sharpe winners (LTCM, MF Global, Volmageddon) were negative-skew ruin. Proven on 2016+ data (SVXY's -83% day). A diagnostic that motivates the ruin-gate.

entries.name: BEDROCK
entries.description: Spread-over-liabilities carry / the insurer's net carry
entries.finding: The duration-neutral credit spread is real but thin (+1.8%/yr), badly negative-skew (-1.96) and crash-correlated; decomposed it is credit beta with ~0 residual alpha. A compensated credit-risk premium, not an edge - the spread is the risk. A liability ingredient.

entries.name: BOOTSTRAP
entries.description: Hedge fund in an ETF / rentable factor beta?
entries.finding: The multi-strategy HF clone is 75% replicable beta with ~0 alpha and lags a 60/40 - 2-and-20 ate the rest (Lo confirmed). The honest exception is managed futures (DBMF): low correlation, a genuine diversifier the linear clone can't capture. Rent that; skip the rest.

entries.name: BUCKLER
entries.finding: The investment side of an annuity is a cheap bond ladder + equity sliver; the ~2.5%/yr variable-annuity wrapper more than halves the return. The one unreplicable value is the mortality credit (longevity pooling) - DIY the investment, buy only the longevity insurance.

entries.name: BOWLINE
entries.finding: Gliding adds no return edge - it matches its own average static allocation, so the timing is neutral. Its real value is sequence-of-returns protection: a -9% late-horizon drawdown vs -17% for a static mix, shielding the largest balance from a late crash. A schedule, not alpha.

entries.name: BELT-TIGHTENERS
entries.description: Inflation domino / sector and global correlation tightening
entries.finding: The proposed inflation domino is plausible, but the test still needs breakeven and CPI data plus enough global history to separate a durable cascade from one episode.

entries.name: BATTERED
entries.description: Distressed survivors / fallen angels / left-tail cost
entries.finding: The hypothesis depends on surviving distress through payout, but liquid ETFs are poor proxies and survivorship is severe. Tradable data has not yet isolated the intended carry.

entries.name: BUREAUCRATS
entries.description: Congressional trading / disclosure and factor test
entries.finding: Public congressional-trading funds have too little history to distinguish information from a technology tilt. A credible test needs transaction-level disclosure data and lag-aware execution.

entries.name: BETS
entries.description: Gambling complex / house premium or consumer beta
entries.finding: The true house edge lives in private prediction and sportsbook data, while listed companies mix that economics with consumer beta. The accessible proxies have not yet isolated the premium.

entries.name: BIGBROTHER
entries.description: Government equity stakes / support versus drag
entries.finding: State ownership could create a backstop premium or an operating drag, but investable events are rare and heterogeneous. The test requires a hand-curated event history rather than a broad industry proxy.

entries.name: BUYOUTS
entries.finding: Private-company performance is not directly observable. The testable residue is post-lockup sponsor behavior, but it still needs a clean event set and realistic borrow assumptions.

entries.name: BACKLASH
entries.finding: Stubbed — the test is blocked on an options open-interest plus intraday feed the public data does not provide.

entries.name: BARRAGE
entries.finding: Stubbed — blocked on an exchange opening-imbalance feed.

entries.name: BEQUEST
entries.finding: Stubbed — blocked on ex-dividend dates and amounts.

entries.name: BIDDING
entries.finding: Stubbed — blocked on an index-rebalance announcement feed.

entries.name: BIGHT
entries.finding: Stubbed — blocked on an options implied-volatility surface.

entries.name: BRANCH
entries.finding: Stubbed — blocked on a supplier/customer relationship graph.

entries.name: BROACHING
entries.finding: Stubbed — blocked on options chains plus an event calendar.

entries.name: BROADCAST
entries.finding: Stubbed — blocked on an earnings/SUE feed.

entries.name: LATAM
entries.finding: While US and commodity beta dominated, the sleeve carried the worst tail and unhedgeable FX, and rotation reduced rather than improved the result. Geography within equities proved to be more beta with a fatter tail.

entries.name: BENEFACTORS
entries.description: Foreign Treasury creditors / causality runs backward
entries.finding: Foreign Treasury flows were weak and coincident; markets and economic conditions often moved before the creditor data. The series is a macro read, not a tradable leading signal.

entries.name: BIND
entries.finding: Liquid hedge-fund replicators delivered watered-down market beta while the true pod-level edge remained private. The useful defensive residues were already represented elsewhere in the family.

entries.name: EMEA
entries.description: US beta / FX drag / no country-rotation edge
entries.finding: Eleven country ETFs collapsed into fewer than two effective bets, dominated by US beta and currency drag. Rotation was negative, so regional labels did not produce real diversification.

entries.name: BULK
entries.finding: Defense stocks behaved as equity beta with a compelling narrative, while geopolitical shocks were priced too quickly for the tested rules. Trend filters added whipsaw rather than protection.

entries.name: BRITTLE
entries.finding: The volatility risk premium was real, but naked short volatility eventually surrendered the carry in the tail. Defined-risk versions then underperformed the index after paying for protection.

entries.name: BIO
entries.description: Biotech dispersion / no systematic price signal
entries.finding: FDA and clinical outcomes created genuine dispersion but were not predictable from price alone. Without domain-specific fundamental data, the sleeve remained a risk diagnostic rather than an edge.

entries.name: BASEL
entries.description: US banks / regulated macro factor / no selection alpha
entries.finding: Seventeen banks reduced to roughly one and a half effective bets, driven by the economy and the short end of the curve. Stock selection and timing added no durable alpha.

entries.name: BELTWAY
entries.finding: Party-aligned baskets often ran opposite the political story as rates and macro conditions dominated. Recent winners also reverted, leaving no stable partisan signal.

entries.name: BURRY
entries.finding: The public style was mostly equity beta; hated-name reversal failed, froth shorts produced ruinous drawdown, and concentration worsened risk-adjusted return. Discretion did not survive systematization.

entries.name: BLANK
entries.description: SPAC decay / borrow and right-tail constraint
entries.finding: Post-merger decay was visible but difficult to short because borrow and the occasional explosive winner dominated execution. The safer trust-carry trade required deal data the public proxy did not provide.

entries.name: BRUTE FORCE
entries.finding: Price and volume alone could not distinguish artificial support from ordinary momentum. Fading the pattern lost money; a credible test would require positioning and flow data.

entries.name: BLURRED
entries.description: Deliberate low correlation / floor rather than edge
entries.finding: Equity correlations shared a common beta and rose precisely when diversification was needed. Low historical correlation was unstable, while pair spreads lacked durable cointegration.

entries.name: BACKSLIDERS
entries.finding: Recent losers tended to bounce, so systematic shorting lost. True terminal declines were obscured by delistings and missing data, implying a fundamental specialist edge rather than a price rule.

entries.name: BUBBLE
entries.finding: AI names formed one crowded growth factor, but price alone could not time its reversal. The practical response is to size and insure the exposure, not mechanically short the story.

entries.name: BRACE
entries.description: Vol-risk-premium harvest / short-vol is the insurer’s side
entries.finding: Listed short-volatility products lagged the index and carried severe negative skew. Regime gates merely exchanged return for drawdown because coincident signals could not defuse the tail.

entries.name: BOUNTY
entries.description: Cross-asset carry / crash-risk premium, not alpha
entries.finding: Liquid carry proxies offered weak excess return, equity correlation, and negative crisis skew. The apparent yield was compensation for crash exposure, not portable alpha.

entries.name: BITE
entries.finding: The public merger-arbitrage proxy earned little over cash while retaining negative skew and crisis correlation. The real edge requires deal selection, leverage, and access the ETF cannot reproduce.

entries.name: BRIDGE
entries.description: Stat-arb / pairs / ideal vehicle, no alpha to carry
entries.finding: The pairs framework achieved neutrality but earned approximately nothing after costs. The vehicle was sound; the historical mean-reversion signal had decayed.

entries.name: BLOATED
entries.description: NVDA capstone bolt-on / higher Sharpe, worse concentration
entries.finding: Adding NVIDIA raised backtested Sharpe but repeated growth exposure already embedded in the capstones and deepened drawdown. The apparent improvement was concentration and sample-period luck, not diversification.

entries.name: BACKFILL
entries.finding: Gap-ups continue rather than revert (+0.08% open-to-close); fading loses net and any snap-back is intraday-only.

entries.name: BANDS
entries.finding: ETF-level curve alpha is a regime-bound short-duration bet, not a durable premium.

entries.name: BANDWAGON
entries.finding: Once crowded via public trackers the edge is gone — NANC/KRUZ track-or-lag SPY; crowded smart money is just beta.

entries.name: BARBICAN
entries.finding: The small-cap January premium has decayed or reversed and the large-cap loser-bounce is noise net of cost, surviving only in untradable illiquid names.

entries.name: BASIC
entries.finding: The ETF-packaged version is equity beta plus a liquidity-crash risk, not a premium.

entries.name: BATON
entries.finding: Macro factor-timing ties but does not beat a static multi-factor blend net of turnover, and fails its one job in 2022 — the factors are the edge, timing them is not.

entries.name: BEACON
entries.description: Kalman dynamic-beta pairs vs static OLS
entries.finding: Dynamic hedging tightens the gross spread but its churn makes it net-worse; neither selection nor the filter earns net on liquid pairs.

entries.name: BEAMING
entries.finding: The headline Sharpe is a daily-bar fill artifact; the executable version is 3x-NDX leverage beta that loses to holding QQQ, and the adaptive layer is overfit.

entries.name: BELLWETHER
entries.finding: The canaries are coincident (same-day corr +0.55), not predictive (next-day -0.02) — the lead-lag is arbitraged away in daily data.

entries.name: BESPOKE
entries.finding: Residualizing gives about the same Sharpe on large caps this window; the documented edge needs a broad/small-cap universe and multi-factor residualization.

entries.name: BEVY
entries.finding: On large-cap, post-2009 price data the momentum crash sits in the winner leg, not a loser squeeze; the thesis needs small-caps and short-interest data.

entries.name: BLEACHER
entries.finding: The brochure's calm window ends the month of Volmageddon; true vol is 33% with a -72% drawdown — the risk limit bounds the loss, not the edge.

entries.name: BLEMISH
entries.description: Is Quality just Value in disguise?
entries.finding: Quality is ~SPY-like in ETF form and the valuation conditioning runs the wrong way; there is no reversal to exploit.

entries.name: BLINK
entries.finding: Real gross, erased net — the overnight-vs-intraday and weekly-reversal edges are the liquidity rent you pay in the spread.

entries.name: BOLLINGER
entries.finding: No directional edge and it loses to holding the stock; the '+899%' headline is beta plus selection, and compression does not even precede expansion at the trade horizon.

entries.name: BOURSE
entries.finding: Carry is thin and crash-prone and trend is too weak on six liquid crosses to stand alone.

entries.name: BOWED
entries.finding: Bond-like return but worse risk-adjusted than bonds, with a -29% equity-correlated crash — levered credit plus duration, not a diversifier.

entries.name: BRIDLE
entries.finding: Low-beta did not beat high-beta in the growth bull; the levered book's Sharpe is residual beta plus leverage, a known weak decade for the factor.

entries.name: BRUNT
entries.description: Skeptic test of a claimed Sharpe>13 factor
entries.finding: Implausible and not reproducible — a faithful price-only analog loses money and the 'drift regime' is just a momentum screen.

entries.name: BUDGET
entries.finding: A window trick plus collateral yield plus a tiny delta; put-selling is the insurer's fat-tail seat, not a free premium.

entries.name: BUNKER
entries.description: Are low-vol stocks a rising-rate bond trap?
entries.finding: Rejected — near-zero daily correlation to Treasuries and no underperformance when rates spike; defensiveness dominates.

entries.name: BURRITO
entries.finding: The testable panic-fade is the known dip-bounce that loses to buy-and-hold, and the policy composite adds nothing atop an untested 'always walks back' assumption.

entries.name: BUZZ
entries.finding: Every live fund underperforms SPY net of its growth tilt and the only 'winners' are delisted mid-sample — the survivorship trap is the finding; raw feeds needed.

entries.name: BYPRODUCT
entries.description: Crypto beyond trend / basis and funding carry
entries.finding: On-screen crypto carry is mostly collateral yield plus a regime-bound basis, not a harvestable premium.

entries.name: BIFURCATE
entries.finding: At the index level credit and equity are coincident, the divergence does not resolve, and the convergence trade inverts — the real edge is issuer-level CDS.

entries.name: BLOODHOUND
entries.description: Credit-to-equity lead-lag / the bond knows first
entries.finding: At the ETF level the credit impulse (high yield minus a duration Treasury) is strongly coincident with equity (+0.72 same-day) but does not lead it (next-day -0.12), and the timing overlay loses to buy-and-hold. The issuer-level diffusion edge needs single-name bonds (bloodhound_2).

entries.name: BROWNSTONE
entries.description: Real estate as an archetype / REITs
entries.finding: Equity REITs are ~0.8 SPY + 0.24 TLT beta with negative residual alpha; adding 10% to a 60/40 lowers its Sharpe. Mortgage REITs are a -70%-drawdown yield landmine and the sub-sectors are one rate factor. A documented beta ingredient, not an edge.

entries.name: BIDE
entries.description: Cash as a position / wait for the fat pitch
entries.finding: The Baupost/Klarman patient-cash posture is dominated by a boring 60/40 on Sharpe (0.59 vs 0.93), return AND drawdown - being 78% in cash is drag. The preservation DNA is real (positive skew) but a bull decade is its worst case, and Klarman's edge is security selection, not cash-timing.

entries.name: BANYAN
entries.description: Endowment model / Yale, in liquid form
entries.finding: The liquid Yale replica is dominated by a boring 60/40 - global equity beta (corr->SPY +0.88, 1.4 effective bets) whose 'alts' are levered equity. It can't buy the real edge (illiquidity, manager selection), which is exactly why Swensen told retail investors to index.

entries.name: BONFIRE
entries.finding: In-sample 'best months' look great but decay out-of-sample (the honest expanding-window test). The physical seasonals (nat-gas winter, gasoline spring) are real but un-harvestable on ETFs - UNG bleeds -22%/yr to contango, swamping the seasonal. The premium lives in the futures curve.

entries.name: BOULEVARD
entries.finding: REIT sub-sectors are one rate factor (1.2 effective bets, +0.78 correlation); a momentum rotation underperforms both an equal-weight basket and simply holding broad REIT, net of cost - value-destroying turnover. You can't rotate within one factor. Confirms brownstone.
